_notes: Italian taxonomy. 10 grammar + 10 vocabulary subs, mirroring FR/PT so the runtime needs no per-language code paths. Italian-specific design choices: (1) past_tenses centers on essere-vs-avere AUXILIARY SELECTION (the biggest IT learner trap — verbs of movement / pronominal take essere; transitives take avere; some verbs alternate by transitivity). Passato remoto is included as a B2/C1 spike only — it is regional and literary, not daily Italian. (2) pronouns_personal carries the ci/ne pair (locative ci, idiomatic ci, partitive ne, causal ne) which has no FR/PT analog. (3) prepositions has heavy emphasis on PREPOSIZIONI ARTICOLATE (al, della, sui, nel, dallo…) — Italian fuses preposition + article aggressively; this is a daily decision point. (4) relative_pronouns is kept (not swapped) because Italian has the che/cui/il-quale triad with 'preposizione + cui' as a real B1-B2 hurdle. (5) complex_sentences includes imperativo (tu/Lei contrast, negative tu = 'non + infinito') and periodo ipotetico (type 1/2/3) — the latter pairs with congiuntivo imperfetto/trapassato. (6) subjunctive (congiuntivo) explicitly includes congiuntivo imperfetto (B2 hypothesis) and congiuntivo trapassato (C1 periodo ipotetico tipo 3). (7) Vocabulary localized: codice fiscale / partita IVA / SSN / INPS / Agenzia delle Entrate / permesso di soggiorno replace FR's CAF / impôts; Trenitalia / Frecciarossa / Regionale / biglietto-da-timbrare replace FR's SNCF terminology; bar (caffè) vs trattoria vs ristorante and primi/secondi/contorni/aperitivo are explicit. (8) register_nuance covers tu vs Lei (the formal-second-person decision that French/Portuguese don't share at this magnitude) plus anglicismi (computer, weekend) and light dialect markers. Pattern list pruned to the questions in this seed bank plus patterns referenced as counterparts/contrast-pairs — no orphans.
